meta.boardNote: The board in the shop numbers its noodles (#1–#16 observed) and lists about 20 cold sides. Numbers here match the board, so a customer can order by number.
sources: Kungfu Noodles — Website Development Documentation (client brief: 4 items)

categories.name: Noodles
categories.blurb: Handmade, cooked to order. The numbers are the ones on the board in the shop — just say the number.

items.name: Kungfu Noodle Special
items.desc: The house dish: chewy hand-pulled noodles in a rich, spicy broth with big chunks of braised buff and a heavy hand of Sichuan pepper. Chicken if you'd rather.
items.source: Tripadvisor feature (Rs 380, 2022); Google review topic “Special Kungfu Noodles”.

items.name: Noodles, Sichuan Style
items.desc: Minced buff, fresh vegetables and numbing Sichuan peppercorns. This is the bowl regulars mean when they say “the Sichuan one”.
items.source: Karl Rock blog (Buff Sichuan Noodles Rs 320); Tripadvisor reviews.

items.name: Chicken & Mushroom Noodles
items.desc: Clear, savoury broth with chicken, shiitake-type mushrooms, greens, garlic and leek. The one to order if you want comfort rather than heat.
items.source: Google review naming “#8, chicken noodle… served with chicken and mushroom”. Price estimated from neighbouring bowls.

items.name: Noodles with Super Spicy Chicken
items.desc: For the heat-seekers: chilli oil, tender chicken and enough Sichuan pepper to make your lips hum.
items.source: Karl Rock blog (Spicy Chicken Rs 240); Google review “#11 noodles with super spicy chicken”; Tripadvisor review ordering it with honey lemon tea.

items.name: Noodles, Wuhan Style
items.desc: Dry-tossed noodles in rich sesame paste with pickled mustard tuber, crushed peanuts and fresh veg. Toss hard before the first bite — no broth here.
items.source: Karl Rock blog (Sesame Wuhan Noodles Rs 320); Google review topic “wuhan style noodles”; Tripadvisor review ordering it mild.

items.name: Hot & Sour Noodles
items.desc: Black vinegar and white pepper, tangy and warming rather than punishing. Ask for it without meat and the kitchen will make it vegetarian.
items.source: Google review “Hot & Sour Noodles (No. 16)”; Tripadvisor reviewer lists #16 as the veg-friendly order. Price estimated.

items.name: Tomato & Egg Noodles
items.desc: Comfort in a bowl: stewed tomato, silky egg, scallion and noodles. No chilli unless you ask for it.
items.source: Photo caption 番茄鸡蛋面 on the Tripadvisor listing; Google review topic “egg and tomato noodle soup”. Price estimated.

items.name: Braised Pork & Beef Noodles
items.desc: Slow-braised pork and beef over noodles in a dark, savoury broth. The richest bowl on the board.
items.source: Photo caption 卤肉牛肉面 on the Tripadvisor listing. Price estimated.

items.name: Special Chinese Dry Noodles
items.desc: Pickled mustard tuber, peanuts, dry noodles and minced meat — the four horsemen, tossed together.
items.source: Tripadvisor feature, Rs 350.

items.name: Three Fresh Vegetable Noodles
items.desc: Garden vegetables in a light broth, no meat. Tell us if you want it properly vegetarian — the wok is shared.
items.source: Photo caption 三鲜蔬菜面 “vegetable noodles” on the Tripadvisor listing. Price estimated.

items.name: Kung Pao Chicken Noodles
items.desc: Wok-fried chicken with dried chillies and roasted peanuts, over noodles.
items.source: Named by a Tripadvisor reviewer (“kung poa noodles”). Number and price to confirm.

items.name: Dan Dan Noodles
items.desc: Minced meat, chilli oil and toasted sesame, tossed so every strand is coated.
items.source: Japanese Tripadvisor reviewer notes タンタンメン (tan tan men) on the menu. Price to confirm.

items.name: Zhajiang Noodles
items.desc: Thick wheat noodles under a glossy fermented bean and pork sauce, with shredded cucumber.
items.source: Japanese Tripadvisor reviewer notes ジャージャー面 on the menu. Price to confirm.

items.name: Chicken Noodles
items.desc: The plain one: chicken and noodles in a clean broth, no chilli unless you ask.
items.source: Ordered by a Tripadvisor reviewer (“chicken noodles”). Number and price to confirm.

categories.name: Cold Counter & Sides
categories.blurb: The half of the menu most people miss. Order two or three for the table while the noodles are pulled.

items.name: Agaric Mushroom with Vinegar
items.desc: Wood-ear mushrooms dressed with black vinegar and garlic. Chewy, cold, refreshing — the classic partner to a spicy bowl.
items.source: Tripadvisor feature: “Agaric and Cucumber served with vinegar, Rs 150 each”.

items.name: Cucumber with Vinegar
items.desc: Seasoned cucumber, garlic and vinegar. The cool-down between bites.
items.source: Tripadvisor feature, Rs 150; myRepublica lists “seasoned cucumbers”.

items.name: Sichuan Style Buff Tongue
items.desc: Cold-sliced buff tongue with chilli oil, toasted sesame and scallion.
items.source: Photo caption 凉拌牛舌 “Sichuan style buff tone” on Tripadvisor; myRepublica lists buff tongue. Price estimated.

items.name: Pork Head Meat in Chilli Oil
items.desc: Cold-sliced pork head meat with chilli oil, coriander and raw garlic. Rich, gelatinous, very Chinese.
items.source: Photo caption 凉拌猪头肉 on the Tripadvisor listing. Price estimated.

items.name: Pig's Ears
items.desc: Super spicy, with coriander and raw garlic. A Thamel cult order — you either get it or you don't.
items.source: Repeated Tripadvisor and Google reviews. Price estimated — to confirm.

items.name: Tripe
items.desc: Cold, chilli-dressed tripe with coriander. Texture is the point.
items.source: Google review “side dishes like peanuts, cucumbers and tripe”. Price estimated.

items.name: Chicken Feet
items.desc: Marinated in chilli and black vinegar, served cold. Chewy and addictive.
items.source: Tripadvisor review “there are chicken feet, pig's ears, tripe…”. Price estimated.

items.name: Pork Paws
items.desc: Braised trotters, sticky and rich, chopped to share.
items.source: myRepublica feature (“not so typical pork paws”). Price estimated.

items.name: Preserved Egg
items.desc: Century egg with pickled ginger and black vinegar. A traditional Chinese side dish.
items.source: Client brief: “Preserved Egg / Buff Salad — traditional Chinese side dishes and cold salads”. Price estimated.

items.name: Salted Egg
items.desc: Salted duck egg, served cold to cut the chilli. A reviewer's favourite.
items.source: Tripadvisor review “salted egg also delicious”. Price estimated.

items.name: Buff Salad
items.desc: Chilled shredded buff with cucumber, coriander, toasted sesame and chilli oil.
items.source: Client brief lists Buff Salad; Google review topic “buff salad” (7 mentions). Price estimated.

items.name: Salted Peanuts
items.desc: Boiled peanuts with star anise and salt — the thing to nibble while you wait.
items.source: Photo caption 盐水花生 on the Tripadvisor listing; Google review mentions peanuts. Price estimated.

items.name: Fried Egg
items.desc: Crisp-edged with a runny yolk. Add it to any bowl.
items.source: myRepublica feature (“typical fried eggs”). Price estimated.

categories.name: Drinks
categories.blurb: Cold, fresh and made to put the fire out.

items.name: Fresh Fruit Juice
items.desc: Pineapple, papaya, mango or watermelon — squeezed to order.
items.source: Tripadvisor review (pineapple, papaya, mango juices). Price estimated.

items.name: Honey Lemon Tea
items.desc: Warm, sweet and sharp. Ordered alongside the super spicy chicken.
items.source: Tripadvisor review “1 honey lemon tea”. Price estimated.

items.name: Canned Iced Tea
items.desc: The imported cans on the shelf — pricey, but they do the job.
items.source: Google review: “Can of tea… 250Rs”.

items.name: Chinese Green Tea
items.desc: A pot of loose-leaf tea, refilled while you eat.
items.source: Common to the shop's drinks list; price to confirm.

items.name: Soft Drinks
items.desc: Chilled bottles, served with a glass.
items.source: Standard bottled drinks; price to confirm.

items.name: Mineral Water
items.desc: One litre, chilled.
items.source: Standard; price to confirm.
